speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have fatigue, flank pain, and fever after recent antibiotics for sinusitis; this could suggest a spread of infection to the kidney. Did the fever start before or after you finished your antibiotic course?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying. Since your sinus symptoms resolved but the fever, fatigue, and flank pain persisted, could you describe the exact location of your pain and if it radiates to your groin or back? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as blood or cloudiness?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the reaction to amoxicillin and your current symptoms, did you experience any burning sensation during urination, urgency, or increased frequency?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, CBC with Differential.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophilic, binucleated cells in your urine stain is highly suggestive of acute interstitial nephritis (AIN), likely triggered by the antibiotic allergy you mentioned earlier. Since your urine culture is negative, this rules out a typical bacterial kidney infection. Have you noticed any new onset rash or hives since the antibiotic was switched to cephalexin?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to antibiotic hypersensitivity.
